policy.rule: A functional item is PASS only when repository evidence plus an exact-head CI run directly proves the declared behavior. Source-code presence alone is not sufficient for browser/Figma runtime behavior.

capture.reason: CI #861 runs the final packaged Standard capture adapter against a real current HTTP document in headless Chrome and repeats document capture 10 times. After removing only volatile capturedAt evidence, all ten snapshots are byte-identical, directly proving deterministic current-document capture for this versioned runtime fixture.
No exact-head automated browser test currently proves successful file:// capture after explicit extension file-access permission.

LocalFolderProvider tests prove document-relative/root-relative resolution, missing-resource reporting, traversal blocking and remote-reference separation; the source-providers suite passed in CI #861.

CI #861 exercises real-browser region capture and proves partial intersections are retained, geometry-free structural ancestors are retained, non-intersecting siblings are excluded, and relationship closure remains valid.

CI #861 uses a real browser fixture with both the document scroll root and a large application scroll container. The final packaged Standard adapter preserves both live scroll positions and marks the qualifying application container as the primary application scroll root.

CI #861 reruns the final packaged Standard adapter in real Chrome against the versioned open-ShadowRoot fixture and preserves host, named slot, source/composed parent, assignedSlotId, and editable shadow/slotted text evidence.

CI #861 reruns the final packaged Standard adapter in real Chrome against the versioned same-origin iframe fixture and preserves the accessible child frame, nested document linkage, editable child-frame text, and absence of false inaccessible-frame diagnostics.

CI #861 runs the final packaged Standard adapter against a real cross-origin iframe boundary. The snapshot records an inaccessible child frame, links STANDARD_CAPTURE_FRAME_INACCESSIBLE to the iframe boundary, and does not fabricate an editable child subtree.

CI #882 runs the final built visual-state runtime in real Chrome 151 and proves CSS/WAAPI animation timelines and geometry plus playing media inside an open ShadowRoot stop while frozen, then resume after restore with zero resume failures and no permanent DOM or inline-state mutation. The exact-head product service worker wraps page/region capture and each responsive viewport capture in the same fail-closed visual-state transaction.

Real headless Chrome/CDP evidence from CI #764 executes the packaged content script and proves cancel and confirm both restore scroll, focus and inline scroll behavior and remove the selector overlay. CI #861 reruns the permanent browser runtime harness successfully.

packageAcceptance.reason: Packager tests prove deterministic .wtf ZIP bytes, manifest/checksums, required payload paths, traversal rejection and canonical JSON; the relevant suites passed in CI #861.
Parser hostile-fixture tests pass and the UI performs parseWtfPackage before enabling renderer handoff. The parser suite reran successfully in CI #861.

CI #798 proves final .wtf export fails closed unless the capture-profile-required reference ground truth is complete. CI #861 reruns the Standard and High Fidelity NODE-14/NODE-21 package validators successfully.

importAcceptance.reason: CI #861 loads the final built Figma plugin UI in real Chrome, uses a trusted CDP pointer click to open the native single-file chooser, assigns a real .wtf archive, securely parses it to preview-ready, preserves choose-source intake metadata and parsed handoff payloads, and emits the render request only after the user import action.

CI #861 executes the final built plugin main bundle unchanged against a narrow simulated Figma host boundary, invokes its registered canvas drop handler with a real .wtf archive, reads the dropped bytes once, preserves canvas-drop source and absolute destination, forwards the bytes to the final built UI in real Chrome, completes secure parsing before enabling import, and uses a trusted pointer import action to emit a render request with the parsed Render Tree, Source Graph and destination intact. The evidence explicitly does not claim Figma Desktop execution.
The UI disables import until parseWtfPackage succeeds, parser hostile fixtures pass, and renderer handoff consumes only currentParsed validated content.
The renderer creates W2F_IMPORTING_ROOT_NAME, marks transactionState importing, then commits after the plan is applied; the behavior is covered by tests.
Injected adapter mutation failure proves the temporary root is removed; the plugin also removes renderedRoot if later hybrid/visual/layout stages fail.
Renderer tests prove semantic names are preserved and blank names receive deterministic useful fallback names.
Tests prove stable source IDs, revision hashes, source tag/selector and document/revision identities are persisted in pluginData.
Capability resolver tests prove native/wrapper/absolute/emulated/raster/unsupported decisions and stable reasons; renderer pluginData preserves render strategy metadata.
Section defaults/normalization and selected-root subtree rendering are directly covered by tests.
Commit calls adapter.setSelection([root]) and adapter.focusNodes([root]); tests assert both calls and the Figma adapter maps them to currentPage.selection and viewport.scrollAndZoomIntoView.

fontAcceptance.reason: CI #781 proves the product renderer uses a deterministic case-insensitive exact family/style decision before any fallback, and the dedicated five-test policy suite verifies exact matches are reported without substitution.
CI #781 proves same-family Regular/nearest/default resolution is explicit and every editable TextNode persists requested-to-chosen font mappings plus reason, count and truncation state in pluginData.
Correction is an allowed strategy, but no tested end-to-end policy currently proves geometry-preserving correction is attempted or validated before a different fallback strategy.

No dedicated policy test currently proves text cannot be rasterized solely to hide missing-font/substitution errors and that raster text is used only when the fidelity profile explicitly justifies it.
